newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Fake bombs sent to ethnic Slovenes in Austria.
newsitem.headline: Fake bombs sent to ethnic Slovenes in Austria.

text.p: Two fake letter bombs accompanied by a note covered in swastikas were found in southern Austria on Friday addressed to ethnic Slovenes, police said.
"The two fakes were identical and made to look like letter bombs," a police spokesman in Klagenfurt in the southern province of Carinthia told Reuters by telephone.
A suspected extreme right organisation warned of a fresh wave of bomb attacks in the runup to European elections on October 13 but no bombs were found.

The group, which calls itself the Bajuwarian Liberation Army, has admitted being behind five series of racist letter bombs which have injured more than a dozen people in Austria and Germany since December 1993.
The packages discovered on Friday had no letter attached, apart from a sheet of paper covered in Nazi swastikas.
One package was sent to Mirko Bogataj, the head of the Slovenian-language section of Austrian state television in Klagenfurt, police said.

The second was addressed to Nuzej Tolmaier, the secretary of the Slovenian Christian cultural association, also based in the Carinthian city. The province borders the former Yugoslav republic of Slovenia.

Police said they had also received a bomb threat directed at a senior political figure in the Carinthia branch of Austria's conservative People's Party. A police official said they had alerted Ferdinand Sablatnig and other politicians in the province to take extra care with their mail.
One police officer was badly maimed in August 1994 while trying to remove a pipe-bomb planted outside a Slovenian-language school in Klagenfurt.
State security officials have linked the waves of bombs with the murder last year of four gypsy men, who were killed in a booby-trapped bomb blast.
Police have come under fire for failing to make any arrests relating to the bombing incidents in the past three years.
